originalTitle: Response content plus one label and one bit reconstructs the ordered journals
originalStatement: E_AB together with r=min(A∖B) and β=1[mex(A)∈B] determines (A,B).
originalHypotheses: Arbitrary finite ordered journals over ℕ and the exact response relation E_AB.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: The response relation E determines I=A∩B because x∉I iff E(x,z) holds for all sufficiently large z (both finite journals eventually omit z).
If r=min(A∖B) is infinite, A=I. Otherwise below r, A membership equals I; r∈A, and for x>r the first clause of E(r,x) is false while the second says x∉A. This reconstructs all A.
Put a=mex(A). Below a every label is in A, so B membership equals I membership. At a the missing bit is preciselyβ=1[a∈B]. For x>a, E(a,x) reduces to x∉B because a∉A. This reconstructs all B.

The two-owner response normal form itself follows by examining the smallest label allowed by at least one owner outsideS. Whichever owner can take it does so, and the other takes the first admissible larger label. This proves the E relation used above.

For alphabet0..M−1 the phase choices give at most2(M+1) pairs. AtM≥2 the unrestricted-response class has A=empty or one singleton and B=empty or{mexA}, all allowed and distinct, attaining the bound. The label and bit are each independently necessary. No storage compression of the potentially quadratic E table is inferred.
